title: Missing semicolon
explanation: In C every statement ends with ;. The compiler often reports it on the line after the one that's missing it.
where: The end of the reported line and the line before it.

pattern: (implicit declaration of function '([^']+)'|call to undeclared function '([^']+)')
title: Function used before it's declared
explanation: C must see a function's declaration before you call it. Include the right header (printf → <stdio.h>, strlen → <string.h>, malloc → <stdlib.h>) or declare your own function above main.
where: The #include lines at the top and the order of your functions.

pattern: format '%([a-z]+)' expects argument of type '([^']+)', but argument \d+ has type '([^']+)'
title: printf/scanf format doesn't match the value
explanation: Each % code must match its argument's type: %d for int, %ld for long, %f for double in printf (%lf in scanf), %c for char, %s for strings.
where: The format string and the matching argument.

pattern: format '%[dfc]' expects argument of type '(int|float|double|char) \*', but argument \d+ has type '(int|float|double|char)'
title: scanf needs an address (&)
explanation: scanf stores into variables, so it needs their addresses: scanf("%d", &x) — not scanf("%d", x).
where: The scanf arguments.

title: Unknown variable
explanation: This name hasn't been declared in this scope. Check spelling, and that it's declared before use and inside the right braces.
where: The first use of the name; where you meant to declare it.

pattern: is used uninitialized|may be used uninitialized
title: Variable used before it has a value
explanation: Local variables in C start with garbage values. Give it a value before reading it (for example int sum = 0;).
where: The declaration of the variable named in the warning.

pattern: suggest parentheses around assignment used as truth value
title: = in a condition (did you mean ==?)
explanation: if (x = 5) assigns 5 to x and is always true. To compare, use ==.
where: The condition on the reported line.

title: gets() is unsafe
explanation: gets() can't limit how much it reads and overflows buffers; it was removed from C. Use fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin) or scanf with a width.
where: The gets call.

title: Something's missing in an expression
explanation: The compiler expected a value here — a missing operand, an extra operator, or a stray symbol.
where: The reported column on that line.

pattern: error: expected (declaration or statement|'}') at end of input
title: Missing closing brace
explanation: A { was opened but never closed with }.
where: Match braces from the top of the function down.

title: Function declared two different ways
explanation: The function's prototype and its definition don't match (different return or parameter types), or it was used before being declared.
where: The prototype and the definition of that function.

title: Wrong number of arguments
explanation: The call passes a different number of arguments than the function takes.
where: Compare the call with the function's definition.

pattern: (incompatible pointer type|makes pointer from integer without a cast|makes integer from pointer without a cast)
title: Pointer/integer type mix-up
explanation: You're mixing a pointer with an integer, or two different pointer types. Check where you need & (address of) or * (value at).
where: Both sides of the assignment or the argument named in the message.

pattern: control reaches end of non-void function
title: Function can end without returning
explanation: A function that returns a value must return on every path, including after loops and in every branch of an if/else.
where: The end of the function and each branch.

title: Unused variable (warning)
explanation: You declared a variable but never used it. Not an error, but often a sign of a typo elsewhere.
where: The declaration of that variable.

pattern: comparison of integer expressions of different signedness
title: Comparing signed and unsigned (warning)
explanation: Comparing an int with an unsigned value (like strlen's result) can behave surprisingly with negative numbers.
where: The comparison on the reported line.

title: Index past the end of an array
explanation: An array of size N has valid indices 0 to N-1.
where: The index and the array's declared size; loop conditions should use < not <=.

title: Segmentation fault
explanation: The program touched memory it doesn't own: an array index out of range, a NULL or uninitialized pointer, or forgetting & in scanf.
where: Array indices, pointers and scanf calls. Try "Check memory" for the exact line.

title: Division by zero (integer)
explanation: Integer division or % by zero crashes the program.
where: Every / and % — check the divisor can't be 0.

title: Program aborted
explanation: Often a buffer overflow detected at runtime (writing past the end of an array or string) or a failed check in free().
where: Writes into arrays and strings; string lengths include the '\0' terminator.

title: Read/write past the end of malloc'd memory
explanation: You accessed memory just outside a block from malloc/calloc. Remember the block holds exactly the bytes you asked for, and strings need one extra byte for '\0'.
where: The first line under 'READ/WRITE of size' in the report that's in your file.

title: Out-of-bounds on a local array
explanation: An index went past the end (or before the start) of a local array.
where: The array access on the line shown in the report.

title: Use after free
explanation: You used memory after calling free() on it. After freeing, don't touch that pointer again (setting it to NULL helps).
where: The 'freed by' and 'previously allocated' stacks show where; then find the later use.

title: Freed twice
explanation: free() was called twice on the same pointer.
where: Every free() call for that allocation.

title: Memory leak
explanation: Memory from malloc was never freed. Every malloc needs a matching free when you're done.
where: The allocation site listed under 'Direct leak'.

title: Signed integer overflow
explanation: The result didn't fit in the type (int holds about ±2.1 billion). In C this is undefined behavior. Use a wider type like long long.
where: The arithmetic on the reported line.

title: NULL pointer dereference
explanation: You used * or -> on a pointer that is NULL — often malloc failed, or a pointer was never set.
where: The pointer used on the reported line; where it should have been assigned.

title: Invalid bit shift
explanation: Shifting by a negative amount or by at least the type's width is undefined.
where: The << or >> on the reported line.

title: Function declared but never defined
explanation: The linker can't find the function's body. Check the spelling matches the definition, and that main is spelled main.
where: The function's name in the call and in its definition.

title: Time limit exceeded
explanation: The program ran too long — usually an infinite loop, or a scanf waiting for input that never arrives.
where: Loop conditions and the loop variable's update.
